lines.text: In April 2003, a twenty-seven-year-old climber named Mr. Aron Ralston set out for a solo adventure in Utah's canyon country.
He didn't tell a single person where he was going.
Deep inside Blue John Canyon, he was squeezing through a narrow slot...
when an eight-hundred-pound boulder suddenly shifted and crushed his right hand against the canyon wall.
He was completely alone. No phone signal. No one knew he was there.
He pushed. He pulled. He chipped at the rock with a cheap pocket knife.
Nothing worked.
By the second day, his water ran out.
By the third day, he was drinking his own urine to stay alive.
He carved his own name and the date he expected to die into the canyon wall.
But on the fifth morning, something changed.
He saw a vision of a little boy... his future son, running toward him.
And in that moment, Mr. Ralston decided: he was NOT going to die in this canyon.
What he did next is almost impossible to believe.
He snapped his own forearm bones by leveraging them against the boulder.
Then, with a dull pocket knife, he cut through his own arm to set himself free.
It took over an hour.
Bleeding and barely conscious, Mr. Ralston rappelled down a sixty-five-foot cliff.
Then he walked eight miles through the blazing desert sun.
A rescue helicopter finally spotted him and rushed him to the hospital.
Against every odd, Mr. Aron Ralston survived.
He didn't just survive. He went back to climbing mountains.
He even climbed all of Colorado's fifty-nine tallest peaks... with one arm.
Some rocks are meant to stop you. Others are meant to show you what you're made of.
